reviewStatus: Drafted from verified sources; pending independent clinician review before clinical release.
commonErrors: Using systolic pressure instead of MAP.
name: Cerebral Perfusion Pressure

version.label: CPP = MAP − ICP
version.detail: Mean arterial pressure minus intracranial pressure, both in mmHg. If MAP is not displayed, it can be estimated as diastolic + (systolic − diastolic)/3.

purpose: Calculates cerebral perfusion pressure from MAP and ICP.
intendedPopulation: Patients with ICP monitoring, e.g. after severe traumatic brain injury.

calculatorNotice.title: Use one reference level
calculatorNotice.message: Arterial transducer levelling (heart or tragus) changes MAP and therefore CPP. Use your unit's convention consistently.

resultStates.label: CPP {total} mmHg
resultStates.detail: Interpret with ICP, MAP trend, autoregulation status and the unit's targets.

clinicalContext.text: CPP is a surrogate for cerebral blood flow when autoregulation is impaired.
Severe TBI guideline context (Brain Trauma Foundation, 4th ed. 2016): CPP 60–70 mmHg recommended as a target range; ICP above 22 mmHg associated with higher mortality.

clinicalInsights.text: ICP is above 22 mmHg, the BTF 2016 threshold associated with increased mortality in severe TBI.
CPP is below the BTF 2016 target range of 60–70 mmHg for severe TBI.
CPP is above 70 mmHg; BTF 2016 notes risk of respiratory complications with aggressive CPP elevation.

limitations.text: A single value; trends and autoregulation matter more than one reading.

limitations: Targets come from severe TBI and may not apply to other conditions.

confounders.effect: Changes MAP and CPP by several mmHg.
Particularly with parenchymal sensors over time.

guideSections.howToPerform: Enter MAP and ICP measured at the same time.
guideSections.clinicalContext: Interpret with trends, autoregulation and guideline targets.

sources.citation: Carney N, Totten AM, O'Reilly C, et al. Guidelines for the management of severe traumatic brain injury, fourth edition. Neurosurgery. 2017;80(1):6-15.
